title: Traffic bleedoff and inflight-preserve emergency SLO guard (hotpatch)
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: intermittent regional reconnections were causing abrupt connection churn and KV-cache loss during rapid failback windows. This increased tail latency and produced SLO violations for a subset of customers during rolling network flaps. This hotpatch introduces a 'traffic bleedoff' path and an inflight-preserve escape hatch that prioritizes completing active KV-backed sessions while gently shedding new requests. The change is intentionally conservative: it nudges circuit thresholds and sashays new-connection admission rather than hard-killing. Key goals: 1) maintain customer-visible session continuity for in-flight requests, 2) reduce SLO noise during short-lived regional instability, 3) provide immediate telemetry to validate efficacy.

release_notes: Hotpatch: introduce a traffic bleedoff coordinator and inflight-preserve escape hatch to reduce SLO violations during short regional reconverges. Defaults are conservative; opt-in canary via runtime flag. Adds metrics: runtime.bleedoff.engaged, runtime.bleedoff.duration_ms, runtime.inflight.pinned_count.
notes_on_implementation: Design summary: The bleedoff coordinator is a thin admission controller inserted at the regional egress gateway. When a region reconverge signal or elevated egress latency is detected, the coordinator enters a bleedoff window: new low-priority requests are placed into a short admission delay (randomized 100-400ms) and then rejected if capacity remains constrained. High-priority/inflight sessions are marked with an ephemeral preserve token; the KV-preserve patch pins the session's small working set and avoids evicting its KV cache for up to 60s or until completion. Circuit reopen backoff was softened: reopen attempts now use an exponential jittered cooldown with a higher base to avoid rapid flip-flopping. Canary rollout: flag runtime.canary.bleedoff enabled for 10% of hosts for 48h, with automated rollback if error budget burn >2*slo_baseline in that window.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests simulate coordinator transitions and validate that pinned inflight sessions are not evicted during reconverge. Integration staging run against a replayed incident trace shows 72% reduction in KV cache miss storms and a 30% reduction in 95th percentile tail latency during brief region flaps. CI initially had a flaky test (coordinator_test.go:TestStagger) failing under race timing; fixed by switching to deterministic clock injection and re-ran pipelines. Load canary in staging for 24h before merging to main.
rollback_plan: Flag-based quick rollback: flip runtime.canary.bleedoff=false for canary hosts; global rollback by disabling bleedoff coordinator at runtime via feature gate. If unexpected persistent errors occur, revert patch and restore previous circuit thresholds. Post-merge monitoring dashboard created and an on-call playbook added to docs/ops/bleedoff-runbook.md.
operational_impact: Expected benign: slight increase in short-term rejection rates for low-priority traffic during bleedoff windows; improved completion rate for inflight sessions. Operators will see new metrics; SRE will evaluate burn rate over the next 72h and may adjust preserve TTL and admission delay windows.
postmerge_actions: 1) Promote console alerts for runtime.bleedoff.engaged to paging at a 10m sustained threshold. 2) Monitor canary host telemetry and collect sample traces where bleedoff engaged. 3) Run a follow-up perf PR to make the pinning lighter-weight if memory pressure observed.
special_notes: This PR is intentionally conservative and contains feature flags for immediate rollback. The implementation avoids broad behavioral changes to eviction policies; instead it biases admission and short-term cache pinning to preserve user-visible sessions. SRE verified the runbook and approved the pager thresholds.
incident_reference: Related to incident SUP-3122 (2026-02-18): regional egress flapping caused repeated KV cache thrash and elevated tail latency. This PR mitigates recurrence for short windows but is not a replacement for long-term egress stability fixes.
